_comment: Optional Claude Code add-ons offered by the Add-ons pane (🧩). The app only ever runs the install commands written here: edit this list to change what it proposes. A missing add-on is pre-ticked when used_by_app or default is true. badge (optional) = a short pill next to the name. check.kind: skill = ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, command = ~/.claude/commands/<name>.md, plugin = <name>@<marketplace> in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, statusline / hook = <name> appears in the statusLine / a hook command of ~/.claude/settings.json. {hooks} in a command = how to run tools/devtools_hooks.py with the Python running Ember (the app itself in a frozen build); {app} = this checkout's folder. needs = programs that must be on PATH first. install.posix runs in the login shell (macOS/Linux), install.windows in cmd.exe; an add-on's lines are joined with && into ONE line, so each must be safe to chain: group any a || b in parentheses, never use cmd's `if` (it swallows the rest of the line), and prefix `claude` with `call` on Windows (npm installs it as a .cmd). reinstall (optional, same shape as install) is what the pane runs when an installed add-on is ticked again; without it, install is re-run. prerequisites: how to install each program listed in needs, per OS (mac / linux / windows); the pane shows the command and can run it in the visible terminal. On Windows without winget (older Windows 10, managed PCs), install["windows-nowinget"] is used when present: the program's official installer, downloaded with PowerShell and opened for the user to click through.

addons.name: graphify
addons.unlocks: Knowledge graph of a project in the Viz pane, and the Build graph button.

posix: uv tool run --from graphifyy graphify install
windows: uv tool run --from graphifyy graphify install --platform windows

posix: uv tool run --from graphifyy graphify install
windows: uv tool run --from graphifyy graphify install --platform windows

addons.name: /improve
addons.unlocks: End-of-session retrospective (the 🔎 button in the Plan pane).

addons.name: ponytail
addons.unlocks: Plugin that pushes Claude toward the smallest code that works. Its hooks run on Node.js.

posix: (claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail || echo marketplace already added)
windows: (call claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail || echo marketplace already added)

posix: (claude plugin uninstall ponytail@ponytail || echo was not installed)
(claude plugin marketplace update ponytail || claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail)
windows: (call claude plugin uninstall ponytail@ponytail || echo was not installed)
(call claude plugin marketplace update ponytail || call claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail)

addons.name: crossref
addons.unlocks: Skill that checks a pasted bibliography against Crossref and finds DOIs.

addons.name: dream
addons.unlocks: /dream consolidates Claude's memory files from recent sessions. Runs on demand; its nightly auto-trigger is set up separately (see its README).

addons.name: Live limits (statusline tee)
addons.unlocks: Usage pane shows Claude Code's own 5-hour and 7-day limit %, reset times, context % and cost instead of the P90 estimate. Your existing statusline keeps working (it is wrapped). Undo: devtools_hooks.py uninstall-statusline.

addons.name: Live activity (hook event tee)
addons.unlocks: An async hook records what each session is doing (tool names, never their inputs) so the sidebar shows live activity and you get a toast when a session waits for your permission. Undo: devtools_hooks.py uninstall-events.

addons.name: Session guards (/careful, /freeze)
addons.unlocks: A PreToolUse hook that makes /careful block destructive shell commands and /freeze block edits outside the folders you name, and logs each block (tool and rule, never the command) to the Guard log in the Config pane. Undo: devtools_hooks.py uninstall-guard.

addons.name: Playwright MCP
addons.unlocks: Microsoft's browser-automation MCP server: Claude can open a page, click through it and read it, e.g. to check an HTML report or a Quarto site it just built. Runs through npx.

posix: claude mcp add --scope user playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest
windows: (call claude mcp remove --scope user playwright >nul 2>&1 || ver >nul)
call claude mcp add --scope user playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest

addons.name: Context7 MCP
addons.unlocks: Up-to-date library documentation pulled into the session (R and Python packages included), so Claude stops guessing at APIs that changed. Hosted server, no key needed; a free key from context7.com raises the rate limit.

posix: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp
windows: (call claude mcp remove --scope user context7 >nul 2>&1 || ver >nul)
call claude mcp add --scope user --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp

windows-nowinget: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = 'Tls12'; $v = (Invoke-RestMethod https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json | Where-Object { $_.lts } | Select-Object -First 1).version; $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('node-' + $v + '-x64.msi'); Invoke-WebRequest ('https://nodejs.org/dist/' + $v + '/node-' + $v + '-x64.msi') -OutFile $f; Start-Process $f -Wait"

note.mac: Needs Homebrew (brew.sh); otherwise use the installer from nodejs.org.
note.linux: Debian/Ubuntu; other distributions: use your package manager.

windows-nowinget: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = 'Tls12'; $r = Invoke-RestMethod https://api.github.com/repos/git-for-windows/git/releases/latest; $a = $r.assets | Where-Object { $_.name -like 'Git-*-64-bit.exe' } | Select-Object -First 1; $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP $a.name; Invoke-WebRequest $a.browser_download_url -OutFile $f; Start-Process $f -Wait"
